approachQuestion.prompt:
Triangular Frames

A workshop has a read-only nondecreasing array lengths of positive integer rod lengths. Count triples of distinct positions i<j<k whose rods can form a nondegenerate triangle. Equal-length rods at different positions are separate rods. Return only the count.

Constraints: 0 <= n = lengths.length <= 4000; 1 <= lengths[i] <= 1000000000. Use signed 64-bit sums and count; the answer fits signed 64-bit. A nondegenerate triangle requires the sum of the two shorter sides to be strictly greater than the longest side.

Example 1: lengths=[2,3,3,4] -> 4.
Example 2: lengths=[1,2,3] -> 0 (equality is degenerate).
Example 3: lengths=[5,5,5,5] -> 4.
constraints: Choose the most efficient valid approach for the entire stated input domain; accept equivalent optimal variants.

options.text: For each longest-side index k>=2, scan l=0 and r=k-1 inward. If lengths[l]+lengths[r]>lengths[k], add r-l and decrement r; otherwise increment l. Sum across all k.
options.feedback: If the smallest current partner works with r, every position between l and r-1 works with r. Each triangle is counted once for its largest index and middle index.

options.text: For every k and j<k, binary-search the first i<j with lengths[i]+lengths[j]>lengths[k], then add the number of such i positions.
options.feedback: The boundary condition and positional count are correct, but each new binary search can be replaced by reusing a moving boundary for that k.

options.text: Use the grouped endpoint count but accept lengths[l]+lengths[r]>=lengths[k].
options.feedback: For [1,2,3], it counts one frame even though the three rods only form a straight line.

options.text: Remove repeated length values, then count value triples that satisfy the triangle inequality.
options.feedback: For [5,5,5,5], four positional triples are valid, but removing repeats leaves too few rods to form any triangle.

feedback.reason: Anchor the longest side and count a whole valid row using a strict inequality while retaining positional multiplicity.
details: For each index k from 2 onward, treat lengths[k] as the longest rod. Scan l=0 and r=k-1. If their sum is strictly larger than lengths[k], add r-l and decrease r; otherwise increase l. Keep duplicate rods as separate positions and accumulate counts across all anchors.
With the largest rod fixed, a successful sum at (l,r) also succeeds for every left index through r-1. Add r-l at once. Equality is not a triangle because the inequality must be strict.

complexityQuestion.prompt: For the fixed method revealed after question 1, choose its tight worst-case time and auxiliary-space pair. Use a word-RAM model with constant-time indexed access and signed 64-bit arithmetic. Include all temporary buffers, input copies, and call frames; exclude supplied input and returned output. n is input length. Output is a single count. The method is iterative with no copied input, result list, recursion, hashing, or amortized operations.
constraints: Analyze this fixed method regardless of your answer to question 1; choose the tightest pair.

options.text: O(n² log n) time, O(1) auxiliary space

feedback.reason: A linear sweep for each largest-rod anchor gives quadratic time.
details: There are n-2 anchors and at most k endpoint advances per anchor. With all lengths equal, each anchor performs k-1 successful grouped counts, giving quadratic worst-case work. Only three indices and a 64-bit accumulator are needed.

“O(n² log n) time, O(1) auxiliary space”: This adds a repeated search factor absent from the fixed scan.
